scope: Targeted primary-source review, prioritizing May-September 2026 papers/revisions and necessary foundations; not an exhaustive literature review or proof of gains in LexiMind.

recommendations.baseline: Keep partial-label supervised losses for book-field heads. Compare admitted generative tasks with SFT, then a compact Dr.GRPO candidate; use DPO separately when genuine preference pairs exist.
optional_objectives: RLP objective with detached observed-token information gain and EMA baseline
recommendations.pretraining: Retain cross-entropy/denoising as controls. Native RPT-style normalized-token continuations and a byte-prefix verifier are prepared; RLP objective/reward/EMA helpers are implemented. Neither is a paper reproduction or evidence that scratch CE can be removed.
recommendations.transfer_limit: The decoder's conditional token probabilities support these objective primitives mathematically; reviewed papers do not demonstrate improvement on LexiMind's custom encoder-decoder or partially labeled book fields.

objective_contracts.notation: m_it selects decoder response tokens; n_i=sum_t m_it; N is response count; G>=2 is a same-prompt rollout group; l, b and f are current, behavior and reference token log probabilities; A and b/f are detached.
objective_contracts.group_advantage: Dr.GRPO: A_i=R_i-mean_g(R). DAPO/GSPO/BPO: divide by explicitly declared group standard deviation for nonflat groups. Reject singleton groups. Equal rewards give zero policy-gradient signal; an explicitly enabled reference penalty can still act.
objective_contracts.standard_deviation: Papers write std without fixing correction. Pin the implementation convention explicitly; the reviewed official verl implementation uses torch.std (sample correction=1) plus a small epsilon. The local primitive uses sample correction=1, exact division for nonflat groups and zero advantages for flat groups. Unequal group-size weighting needs its own contract.
objective_contracts.dr_grpo: rho_it=exp(l_it-b_it); L=-sum_it m_it*min(rho_it*A_i,clip(rho_it,0.8,1.2)*A_i)/(N*fixed_response_cap). The fixed cap must not change with padding.
objective_contracts.dapo_style: Use standardized group advantages and token-mean clipped loss; paper clipping interval [0.8,1.28]. This branch does not implement dynamic resampling or overlong reward shaping.
objective_contracts.gspo: s_i=exp(sum_t m_it*(l_it-b_it)/n_i); L=-mean_i min(s_i*A_i,clip(s_i,0.9997,1.0004)*A_i). The geometric-mean surrogate is not an exact whole-trajectory importance ratio.
objective_contracts.bpo_experimental: omega_it=(1+0.1-exp(b_it))/(1+0.1-exp(l_it)); M=0 if A_i>0 and omega>1+clip_high, or A_i<0 and omega<1-clip_low; otherwise M=1. L=-mean_i sum_t m_it*A_i*M_it*stopgrad(min(omega_it,3))*l_it/n_i. Require explicit clip widths; paper does not state BPO values unambiguously.
objective_contracts.sampled_reference_penalty: k3=expm1(f_it-l_it)-(f_it-l_it). Optional beta defaults to zero. Under behavior-policy samples this is a sampled penalty, not an unbiased measured current-policy KL; no silent importance-correction or overflow clamp.
objective_contracts.dpo: L=-mean log_sigmoid(beta*((sum_m l_chosen-sum_m l_rejected)-(sum_m f_chosen-sum_m f_rejected))). Original DPO uses response log-probability sums, not length means; chosen/rejected must refer to the same prompt and a documented preference.
objective_contracts.numerical_and_sampling: Compute log-softmax/reductions in stable precision; reject nonfinite active values and importance-ratio over/underflow. Preserve tokenizer/model revisions, actual sampling distribution, temperature, EOS and truncation. The prepared adapter supports an explicit positive temperature with full categorical support only (top-p=1, top-k=0); policy/behavior and reference temperatures must agree. No implicit replay or truncation correction.
objective_contracts.rlp: A_i=G/(G-1)*(R_i-mean_g(R)), with equal per-thought means of clipped token losses and no KL in the core recipe. Clip widths must be supplied explicitly; reviewed paper does not state numeric values. Information gain is detached logp(observed target|context,thought)-logp(observed target|context;EMA), returned per observed position without automatic span averaging.
objective_contracts.native_adapter: Cached native sampling stores actual full-support temperature log probabilities, response-only masks including first EOS, stop status and tokenizer/special-token/precision contracts. Teacher-forced scoring retains active PAD tokens, skips unused response capacity and shares prompt encoding. Dropout and ambient autocast are disabled consistently; current eval-mode scoring also disables native gradient checkpointing. Initial Trainer integration requires gradient_accumulation_steps=1 because existing microbatch-mean accumulation differs from merged token/response-weighted objectives. PCGrad projects only the encoder; decoder/head gradients are summed. GPU numerical parity, precision/memory feasibility and throughput remain unmeasured.

reward_contracts: A reward record needs task/prompt/response identity, source and split/group provenance, verifier ID/revision, evidence digest, score or explicit unscored status, and termination/truncation status.
Unknown book labels remain unknown; do not manufacture negatives, preference pairs, full-set F1 rewards, or correctness labels from unreviewed agent suggestions.
CR4 free-form human responses require task/ontology adjudication before becoming categorical rewards; plausible alternative emotions are not automatically incorrect.
Formatting, exact string match and outcome correctness are different reward components. Do not reward verbosity or JSON validity as a substitute for supported book content.
For RPT, verify raw continuation bytes and ground-truth token boundaries with a pinned tokenizer; generic whitespace/case normalization changes the task.
For RLP, isolate sampled thought-token masks, future target tokens and a pinned context-only EMA baseline; reward construction cannot expose target continuation as input.

Audit verifier-accepted errors on an independent human-reviewed holdout. Log reward, valid coverage, zero-advantage rate, clip fraction, response length, truncation, sampled KL and actual generated tokens separately.
Any future experiment needs admitted data, available hardware, a total compute budget, matched controls, group-safe splits and existing execution admission. This register grants none of these.

The four-work RPT pilot explicitly uses tokenizer-normalized, stable round-trip continuation bytes. It is separately named from raw-byte RPT corpus reproduction; all work partitions and per-source licenses remain attached.

sources.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
sources.finding: Group-relative rewards replace a learned critic. The sampled reference penalty is exp(logref-logpolicy) - (logref-logpolicy) - 1.
sources.decision: Shared group-advantage and sampled-penalty primitives. An old-policy sample does not make this an unbiased current-policy KL measurement.

sources.title: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective
sources.finding: Removes reward-standard-deviation scaling and response-length division; a fixed generation cap supplies loss normalization. Appendix G uses symmetric 0.2 clipping and zero KL coefficients.
sources.decision: Preferred simple RL objective candidate. No claimed gain for LexiMind; retain supervised controls and record response length.

sources.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
sources.finding: Token-mean policy loss, higher upper clipping, dynamic sampling, and truncation handling form a combined system. Paper clipping is 0.2 below and 0.28 above one.
sources.decision: Prepare DAPO-style token loss only. Dynamic sampling needs an explicit rollout cap and accounting for rejected groups; do not call one loss branch a full DAPO reproduction.

sources.title: Group Sequence Policy Optimization
sources.finding: Clips the geometric mean of token probability ratios once per response, with standardized group advantages. Its reported lower/upper clipping widths are 0.0003/0.0004.
sources.decision: Optional shared objective for sequence rewards. Do not copy token-level clipping defaults; MoE reasoning results do not establish encoder-decoder transfer.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
sources.finding: Directly fits chosen-versus-rejected response preferences against a frozen reference using a logistic loss on sequence log-probability differences, without online RL rollouts.
sources.decision: Prepare a small offline preference objective alongside RL. Requires admitted preference pairs; free responses or partial class labels are not preference pairs.

sources.title: Faster Synchronous On-Policy RL via Straggler-Aware Group Sizing
sources.finding: A CPU controller adjusts group size from rollout-length statistics. Studies use 3B models on a 141GB H200; equal per-step generations do not imply equal total optimizer steps.
sources.decision: Record rollout lengths and generated tokens now. Defer dynamic group control until generation is a measured bottleneck and group weighting is specified.

sources.title: Rollout-Level Advantage-Prioritized Experience Replay for GRPO
sources.finding: Reuses individual high-advantage rollouts with age eviction while retaining all fresh on-policy samples. Gains depend on model and sampling regime; an 8B extension uses one seed and a different batch.
sources.decision: Defer replay. Preserve behavior-policy revision, behavior log probabilities, age, sampling probabilities, and fresh/replay identity before considering it.

sources.title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
sources.finding: One rollout per prompt is supported by value-model training, two critic updates per policy update, and strict clipping under policy lag. Main experiments use Qwen3-30B-A3B and long agentic trajectories.
sources.decision: Defer asynchronous actors and critics. This is not group-size-one GRPO and is not a demonstrated low-compute recipe for LexiMind.

sources.title: Policy Improvement Reinforcement Learning
sources.finding: Uses feedback about improvement against historical performance to modulate base policy-optimization signals. July is a revision, not its first publication.
sources.decision: Track independent validation and historical checkpoints. Do not implement the controller from an abstract-level review.

sources.title: Bellman Policy Optimization
sources.finding: Uses detached capped complementary-probability weights, omega=(1+epsilon-p_old)/(1+epsilon-p_current), instead of ordinary importance ratios. Clip masks also use omega. Appendix B specifies sequence-mean/token-mean reduction, epsilon=0.1, cap=3, and no KL.
sources.decision: Small experimental objective only, disabled by default. Require explicit lower/upper clipping because BPO values are not explicitly reported. Ideal-objective equivalence is not a guarantee for the approximate implemented loss; evidence centers on Qwen3 math.

sources.title: Verifier Errors in RLVR: Reward Hacking, Limits of Feedback, and Selective Control
sources.finding: Studies when imperfect-verifier reward improves while actual correctness declines, and why extra correctness audits are needed to identify accepted errors.
sources.decision: Keep reward provenance, verifier revision, independent held-out correctness checks, and unscored unknowns. No implementation of its selective-control algorithm is claimed.

sources.title: GRPO Training Dynamics for Small Language Models
sources.finding: Studies 1.5B-7B models with 8xA100 and two seeds; group-size gains vary by model. Reported out-of-distribution improvements occur in about 80% of math configurations but about 39% of MCQ configurations.
sources.decision: Use task-specific controls and paired seeds; larger groups and RL are not automatically better. The paper's small-model compute setting is much larger than an unprovisioned laptop.

sources.title: Reinforcement Pre-Training
sources.inspected: method, verification rule and experiment setup
sources.finding: Recasts continuation prediction as RL with byte-prefix correctness ending at an actual ground-truth token boundary. Experiments start from a 14B distilled reasoner with eight rollouts, rather than a random initial model.
sources.decision: Prepare a continuation-verifier contract only. A generic normalized-string exact-match score is not this reward, and success does not establish replacement of initial cross-entropy pretraining.

sources.title: RLP: Reinforcement as a Pretraining Objective
sources.finding: Rewards sampled thoughts by future-token log-likelihood gain over a context-only EMA policy. Uses leave-one-out scaling G/(G-1), no group standard-deviation scaling, and a clipped loss only on thought tokens. Its continued-pretraining phase excludes ordinary next-token cross entropy.
sources.decision: Record a future information-gain reward interface, separate thought masks and EMA checkpoint. Requires trained base models and target-only future tokens; do not leak the continuation into encoder inputs.

sources.title: Reinforcement Learning on Pre-Training Data
sources.finding: Autoregressive and masked-segment reasoning use a generative reward model for semantic prefix equivalence after a cold-start instruction stage.
sources.decision: Keep distinct from RPT and RLP. Defer learned semantic graders; this is not a teacher-free rule-verifiable exact-match recipe.

sources.title: RL Excursions during Pre-Training: Re-examining Policy Optimization for LLM training
sources.finding: Tests RL at intermediate checkpoints of 1B/4B OLMo2-style math-heavy pretraining. Parallel SFT/RL averages separate optimizer updates; the body reports stronger pass@32 with lower pass@1 than direct RL/SFT in that comparison.
sources.decision: Preserve intermediate checkpoints, pretraining-token accounting, SFT/RL controls and separate pass@1/pass@k. A combined scalar loss or gradient sum is not the paper's parallel-update method.

sources.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
sources.finding: Studies 5M-1B chess models with an 81-token vocabulary and verifiable puzzles, plus a 1B math transfer experiment. Better pretraining predicts stronger subsequent RL; more pretraining can remain competitive at pass@16.
sources.decision: Budget and compare pretraining against RL jointly. Small chess models are relevant mechanistic evidence, not measured scaling laws for book classification.

sources.title: RL Starts before RL: On Policy Distillation for Better Reinforcement Learning
sources.finding: Studies 8B students with 32B teachers and full teacher distributions. Distillation-objective rankings can change after RL; initial pass@k does not fully predict final gains.
sources.decision: Future optional initialization control. Teacher generation/distribution access and their full compute costs are prerequisites, not part of the current preparation.

implementation_reference.scope: Group standard-deviation convention only; mutable upstream code is not a pinned dependency or a claim of experiment reproduction.

implementations.execution: disabled; no training or model-quality evaluation
